pain_points.description: The 'do X on PASS, Y on FAIL' branching limitation forces an awkward shape for a 'cancel on FAIL, commit+push on PASS' flow. The canonical pattern (check.on_fail: cancel, success-path downstream) works, but it means failure semantics are implicit (the run just halts) rather than explicit. A worked example of a PASS/FAIL gate-then-act flow in AUTHORING.md would have saved a re-read of the §10 pitfall row.

worktree.cleanup with policy: merge_to_base is described as fast-forwarding the base branch, but it isn't obvious whether the commit needs to be pushed to origin first or whether the engine pushes the resulting fast-forward of base. Had to assume an explicit 'git push' in the commit step is still required for the remote, and that cleanup handles the base-branch ff locally (and presumably pushes it — unclear). A one-line clarification of what cleanup pushes vs. what the workflow must push would help.

$-substitution table doesn't mention multi-line command: blocks with embedded $state/$inputs. Worked by analogy with the single-line command: row, but a tiny note ('substitution applies to the whole scalar, including |-block scalars') would remove the doubt.

Defaults list says allowed_tools defaults to [Read, Grep, Glob]. For an investigate step those defaults are perfect, but it isn't stated whether providing allowed_tools merges with or replaces the defaults. Assumed 'replaces' and listed all tools explicitly — but a one-word clarification ('replaces') would be nice.

Enum-on-string fields use the inline-flow form ({type: string, enum: [PASS, FAIL]}) in §5's example and the block form in §3 example 3. Both work, but the inconsistency made me double-check whether one was preferred.

self_assessment: The workflow follows AUTHORING.md conventions: four logical stages, worktree.create + worktree.cleanup bracketing the run, a check gating on review status with on_fail: cancel per the §10 pitfall guidance. The main authoring friction was the missing first-class PASS/FAIL branching primitive — solved with the documented cancel-on-fail pattern, but it leaves the FAIL path implicit rather than explicit. Otherwise AUTHORING.md was sufficient to author the workflow end-to-end without consulting SPEC.md or harness source.
